title: Interview: pantry model
lead: Decide how "probably in the house" is estimated and corrected (N1–N4).

sections.heading: Why
sections.body: Estimates need defaults (shelf lives, usage) that only the household knows, such as how fast it goes through milk or pet food.

sections.heading: Owner input
sections.body:
1. Shelf-life defaults per category; overrides for specific items?
2. Recipe consumption: when a meal is marked "made", subtract its ingredients from the estimate (recommended)?
3. Which taps to offer: "used it up", "tossed it", "plenty on hand"? Where: on the list or a pantry page?
4. "Use it up" nudges: how many days before the estimated expiry? Show them on the Today view?
5. Runout predictor items: which pet and household staples? Lead time before running out?

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Ask the questions, using real order history from the samples as examples.
2. Write ADR 0023; record the raw answers in `local/` (not committed).
3. Update the pantry slices (`slicer edit`).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: - ADR 0023 has the default tables and the tap/nudge decisions.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: Commit only when the owner asks; no AI attribution.
